sentences.en: My friend Xiao Li had been job-hunting for a long time, and hadn't found one.
Last week, he went to interview at a company.
Yesterday, the company called and told him he could start work.
Xiao Li was so happy, he called me right away and told me the good news.
I said: "Congratulations, you finally found a job!"
In the evening, a few classmates treated him to a meal together, and everyone said to him: "Congratulations!"
Xiao Li raised his glass: "Thank you all — next one's on me."

quiz.q: Why had Xiao Li been unhappy before the good news?
a: He had been job-hunting for a long time without success

quiz.q: What does the narrator say when Xiao Li shares his news?
a: Congratulations, you finally found a job!

quiz.q: What does Xiao Li promise at the end?
a: To treat everyone to a meal next time

grammar.e: 恭喜 is used to congratulate someone on good news — finding a job, passing an exam, getting married, or having a baby. Add 你 to speak directly to the person, or just say 恭喜恭喜 to a group.
grammar.x: 恭喜你，终于找到工作了！— Congratulations, you finally found a job!

grammar.e: 找 means 'to look for', but 到 after it shows the search succeeded — 找到 means 'found it', while 没找到 means 'didn't find it.'
grammar.x: 他找了很久，一直没找到。— He looked for a long time, and hadn't found one.

grammar.p: verb + 了 + duration (how long you did something)
grammar.e: Put 了 right after the verb, then add how long — 找了很久 means 'looked for a long time.'
grammar.x: 他找工作找了很久。— He had been job-hunting for a long time.
